message.text: The new wrapper turns only a LostLock into exit 2 and rethrows every other error. No test makes `measureHeld` throw anything other than a LostLock, so the narrowing is never checked. No test in `packages/evals/test/parity.test.ts` would fail with the ConditionalExpression→false mutant on line 437 (or the BooleanLiteral mutant there) or with the rethrow on line 438 deleted. A search for rejects/toThrow in that file found none.

explanation.what: The new wrapper turns only a LostLock into exit 2 and rethrows every other error. No test makes `measureHeld` throw anything other than a LostLock, so the narrowing is never checked. No test in `packages/evals/test/parity.test.ts` would fail with the ConditionalExpression→false mutant on line 437 (or the BooleanLiteral mutant there) or with the rethrow on line 438 deleted. A search for rejects/toThrow in that file found none.
explanation.whatToDo: Add a test where `runners.range` (or `models`) throws an ordinary Error. Assert that `measureParity` rejects with that error and that the lock is released.
explanation.whyHere: Before this change, an unexpected error such as a failing runner or a failed save escaped measureParity. With either mutant it becomes exit 2 with a printed message, which a caller reads as a configuration refusal. That would hide crashes.

properties.failureScenario: Apply `if (false) throw thrown;` on line 437. Have `range` throw `new Error("boom")`. measureParity now returns 2 and prints "boom" instead of rejecting. Every test in parity.test.ts still passes, because none has a non-LostLock error escape (I inferred this from the search finding no rejects or toThrow).
